entries.title: actix/actix-web — Powerful, pragmatic, extremely fast Rust web framework
entries.note: Maintained under the Actix org; MIT-or-Apache-2.0 dual-licensed. README documents 4.x series and Rust 1.75+ MSRV.

entries.title: actix-web — crates.io (68M+ downloads)
entries.note: Latest stable: 4.13.0 (Feb 2026). 68M+ all-time downloads. Still no 5.0; the 4.x series remains the active line.

entries.title: Actix Web — official documentation
entries.note: Primary docs site for getting-started, routing, extractors, and middleware patterns.

entries.title: Actix-web vs Axum in 2026 — throughput, latency, memory
entries.note: 2026 head-to-head: Actix ~20k req/s vs Axum ~18k req/s; idle RAM 50–80 MB (Actix) vs 60–90 MB (Axum). Actix wins raw throughput; Axum wins maintainability for most teams.

entries.title: Rust Web Frameworks in 2026: Axum vs Actix vs Rocket vs Warp vs Salvo
entries.note: Survey of the 2026 Rust web-framework landscape; Actix retains the raw-perf crown, Axum dominates new-project mindshare.

entries.title: Rust Web Development 2026 — Actix, Axum, and Modern Rust
entries.note: Hands-on 2026 guide covering production patterns for Actix and Axum.

entries.title: Keats/tera — Jinja2/Django-style template engine for Rust
entries.note: v1 frozen, v2 on crates.io with migration guide. MIT-licensed. Maintained by Vincent Prouillet (also author of Zola).

entries.title: Tera — official site and docs
entries.note: Runtime template engine modeled on Jinja2/Django. Supports inheritance, macros, filters, tests; templates loaded from disk at startup or via glob.

entries.title: tera — crates.io
entries.note: v2 generally-available; v1 frozen. Tera ships an auto-reload feature that recompiles templates on file change for dev workflows.

entries.title: askama-rs/askama — type-safe compile-time Jinja-like templates
entries.note: Generates Rust code from templates at compile time. The rinja fork was re-unified with Askama in 2024–2025.

entries.title: Askama — official introduction
entries.note: Templates are bound to user-defined structs; #[derive(Template)] gives you typed render() methods and compile-time errors for missing fields.

entries.title: askama 0.14.0 on docs.rs
entries.note: 0.14.0 released 2025-04-23. Note: the standalone askama_actix integration crate was deprecated/removed in 0.13; use Askama's core Template::render() and return a string body.

entries.title: askama_actix on Lib.rs — marked deprecated/not recommended
entries.note: Confirms 0.15.0+deprecated status; new code should call .render() directly and return HttpResponse::Ok().content_type("text/html").body(html).

entries.title: lambda-fairy/maud — compile-time HTML templates as a Rust macro
entries.note: Alternative to Tera/Askama. Templates are inline Rust macros, not external files — IDE-friendly but designer-hostile.

entries.title: Rust Template Engines: Compile-Time vs Run-Time vs Macro Tradeoffs
entries.note: Clear taxonomy: Tera = runtime, Askama/Maud = compile-time. Compile-time gives type safety + speed but requires a recompile per template change unless dev-mode auto-reload is wired up.

entries.title: actix-sse-example — broadcast SSE with actix-web
entries.note: Canonical pattern: tokio broadcast channel + actix-web-lab Sse helper + 10s heartbeat ping to evict stale clients.

entries.title: actix_web_lab::sse — official SSE helper module
entries.note: Sse::from_infallible_receiver, Sse::from_stream, retry/keepalive helpers — first-party SSE story for Actix in 2026.

entries.title: htmx ~ Server-Sent Events extension
entries.note: hx-ext="sse" + sse-connect="<url>" + sse-swap="<event>" wires a server stream into any DOM element. ~12 KB JS, no build step.

entries.title: HTMX vs Alpine.js — Lightweight Interactivity 2026 (PkgPulse)
entries.note: HTMX = server-driven HTML swaps; Alpine = client-side reactive state. Most 2026 lightweight stacks use both together.

entries.title: The HARM Stack (HTMX + Axum + AlpineJS + Rust + Maud)
entries.note: Worked example of a Rust SSR + HTMX + Alpine stack; demonstrates the architecture in production.

entries.title: tray-icon — crates.io (Tauri-org maintained)
entries.note: 1.87M downloads/month, used by 149 crates. macOS main-thread requirement; Linux uses libayatana-appindicator or libappindicator. Latest update Apr 2026.

entries.title: tray_icon — docs.rs API reference
entries.note: Cross-platform tray icon + menu API; standalone from Tauri and usable in any Rust app with a winit event loop.

entries.title: Zola — uses Tera templates
entries.note: Reference production user of Tera. Tera's primary author Vincent Prouillet built Zola; the two evolve together.

entries.title: Jellyfin — networking and bind-address docs
entries.note: Reference architecture for a localhost-or-LAN web app: HTTP on 8096, no native window, served to any browser on the network.

entries.title: DNS rebinding attacks explained — GitHub Security blog
entries.note: Threat model that any localhost web service must defend against. Mitigation: bind 127.0.0.1 only AND validate Host header AND require a bearer token.

entries.title: Making PWAs installable — MDN
entries.note: Chrome/Edge desktop install puts the PWA in the macOS dock or Linux app launcher with standalone display-mode. Path to a 'feels like an app' UX without shipping a native window.

entries.title: Pi-hole v6 — setting and using the web password
entries.note: Real-world prior art for a localhost web admin UI with bearer/password auth — Pi-hole's approach to the same UX problem MCP Manager faces.

entries.title: watchexec/cargo-watch — releases and usage
entries.note: cargo watch -x run gives a 2–4s rebuild loop. Combined with Tera auto-reload, dev iteration on templates is near-instant; with Askama, every template change triggers a full rebuild.

entries.title: Actix Web — Auto-Reloading documentation
entries.note: Official guide to combining cargo-watch with systemfd/listenfd for graceful socket-passing restarts on file change.

entries.title: Seamless Server-Side Templating in Rust — Askama and Tera
entries.note: Side-by-side recipes for both engines including Actix integration patterns post-askama_actix-deprecation.

entries.title: Boringcactus 2025 Rust UI survey — 43 libraries tested
entries.note: Referenced by sister stacks. The browser itself trivially passes the screen-reader + IME test that 94% of Rust GUI toolkits failed, which is the strongest single argument for the SSR stack.

entries.title: actix-web-lab — crates.io
entries.note: Maintained by the Actix team as a staging ground for features (SSE, typed headers, scope guards). Promoted features eventually move into actix-web proper.
